interface.space: Symmetric N-boson wave functions in L2(R^(3N))
interface.potential: V >= 0, smooth, radial, compactly supported; source requires its dimensionless rho to be sufficiently small
interface.scattering: (-Delta + V/2)f0=0, f0 -> 1, a0=lim |x|(1-f0); scattering length of N^2 V(Nx) is a0/N
interface.initial_data_high_moments: For every m>=1, <psi_N,H_N^m psi_N> <= C^m N^m and fixed-k marginals condense to |phi><phi| tensor k
interface.initial_data_low_energy: <psi_N,H_N psi_N> <= C N and for every fixed k, ||psi_N - phi tensor k tensor xi_N^(N-k)|| -> 0
interface.observable: Fixed-k reduced density gamma_N,t^(k), tested against compact J^(k) on L2(R^(3k))
interface.time: Every fixed real t; convergence is locally uniform on compact time intervals for each fixed k

claims.claim: Under the stated repulsive GP scaling, energy and condensation assumptions, every fixed-k reduced density converges to the factorized solution of the cubic GP equation with coefficient 8*pi*a0.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed k and each fixed t in R; the source proves compact-time convergence in the fixed-k weak* metric.

claims.claim: The exact scattering rescaling gives coefficient 8*pi*a0: N V_N(x) f_N(x) converges distributionally to 8*pi*a0 delta_0.
claims.quantifiers: Fixed smooth compactly supported radial V; f_N(x)=f0(Nx); N tends to infinity.
claims.proof: Change variables y=Nx and use integral V(y)f0(y)dy=8*pi*a0.

claims.claim: The cutoff H^k estimate supplies the hierarchy regularity needed for uniqueness.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed integer k, rho sufficiently small, ell >> N^(-1/2), and N >= N0(k,C0).
claims.estimate: <psi,(H_N+N)^k psi> >= C0^k N^k integral Theta_(k-1)^(k)|nabla_1...nabla_k psi|^2 plus nonnegative derivative and potential terms.
claims.cutoff_window: Choose N ell^2 -> infinity, N ell^3 -> 0, and N ell^(3-epsilon) -> 0; ell=N^(-2/5), epsilon=1/4 is admissible.
claims.limit_consequence: Tr product_j(1-Delta_j) gamma_infinity,t^(k) <= C1^k with C1 independent of k and t on fixed compact intervals.
claims.source: Annals 2010, Proposition 5.3, Proposition 6.3, equations (5.29)-(5.33) and (6.12)-(6.13); uniqueness: arXiv:math-ph/0508010 v3, Theorem 9.1.

claims.claim: The proof's cutoff estimate is a fixed-k limit and does not provide a prelimit bound uniform for k growing with N.
claims.quantifiers: The estimate has N0=N0(k,C0), cutoff exponent 2^k*ell^(-epsilon), and Prop. 6.3 takes N to infinity for each fixed k.
claims.consequence: Do not interchange the fixed-k limit with a supremum over 1<=k<=N.

claims.claim: At the matched weaker-interaction scaling 0<beta<1/2 with the same V and product initial state, the effective coefficient is integral V rather than 8*pi*a0.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed beta in (0,1/2), under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1 of the primary baseline source.
claims.source: Erdos-Schlein-Yau, arXiv:math-ph/0508010 v3, Theorem 1.1; Annals 2010, Section 2.

claims.claim: No universal algebraic fixed-k convergence rate follows from the qualitative initial condensation and O(N) energy assumptions of Theorem 2.2.
claims.quantifiers: There is no delta>0 and universal constant bounding all admissible one-body errors by O(N^(-delta)).
claims.counterexample: For orthonormal smooth compactly supported phi,chi, set phi_N=sqrt(1-epsilon_N^2)phi+epsilon_N chi and psi_N=phi_N tensor N, with epsilon_N=1/log(N+2). Then the energy is O(N), the fixed-k strong factorization holds, and the one-body trace-norm error at t=0 is exactly 2/log(N+2).

claims.claim: Uniform-in-k convergence over every 1<=k<=N is false even within the low-energy theorem's initial-data class.
claims.quantifiers: A single admissible sequence has sup_(1<=k<=N) trace-norm error bounded away from zero at t=0.
claims.counterexample: Use the same product family with epsilon_N=N^(-1/2). For k=N, the trace-norm distance from |phi tensor N><phi tensor N| is 2*sqrt(1-(1-1/N)^N), tending to 2*sqrt(1-e^(-1)).

falsifier.target_stronger_claims: A universal algebraic convergence rate from only qualitative condensation, or convergence uniformly over all k<=N.
falsifier.decisive_observation: Both failures occur at t=0 for the explicit smooth product sequences in C6 and C7, which satisfy the O(N) energy and fixed-k factorization assumptions.

primary_sources.authors: L. Erdos, B. Schlein, H.-T. Yau
primary_sources.title: Derivation of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for the dynamics of Bose-Einstein condensate
primary_sources.date: arXiv v3 dated 2006-12-10; Annals of Mathematics 172 (2010), 291-370

primary_sources.authors: L. Erdos, B. Schlein, H.-T. Yau
primary_sources.title: Derivation of the cubic non-linear Schrodinger equation from quantum dynamics of many-body systems
primary_sources.relevant_result: Theorem 1.1 gives the beta<1/2 product-state Born baseline; Theorem 9.1 gives uniqueness in the hierarchy class with C^k weighted Sobolev bounds

unresolved: No independent full proof audit of the long induction in Proposition 5.3 or every passage in Section 7 was completed.
No quantitative rate for later-time convergence under an explicit initial condensation modulus was derived.
No novelty or priority claim is made.
